notes.text: For more than 8, cook the potatoes in two batches so they crisp instead of steaming.

callback.body: Rolling something tight works the same with any wrapper: filling near the bottom edge, the sides tucked toward the middle, then roll away from you and keep it snug. Today the wrapper is a big, soft tortilla.

move.title: Slowest first, fastest last
move.body: Timing a meal means planning which part to start first so everything is hot at the same moment. Today you'll cook crispy potatoes, turkey sausage, and scrambled eggs, one after another in the same pan, then roll them with cheese into big breakfast burritos.

why.title: Slowest first
why.body: Potatoes take about 15 minutes. Sausage takes about 7. Eggs take 3. Start the slowest and end with the fastest, and the eggs come out of the pan just as you're ready to roll, while the potatoes are still warm.

why.title: Keep the finished parts warm
why.body: Food loses heat fast in the open air. A bowl covered with foil holds the heat in while you cook the next part, so nothing is cold by the time you roll.

why.title: Steam, then crisp
why.body: With the lid on, the potatoes steam and soften inside. With the lid off, the water leaves and the outsides turn golden and crisp. Soft middle, crunchy outside.

why.title: Warm tortillas bend
why.body: A cold tortilla is stiff and cracks when you fold it. A little warmth and steam make it soft and stretchy, so it wraps around the filling without tearing.

wrong.sign: The tortilla cracks when you fold it
wrong.fix: Warm it a little longer, wrapped in a damp towel, so it softens.
Use a little less filling, tuck the bottom edge tight before you roll, and set it seam side down.

wrong.sign: The potatoes are still hard in the middle
wrong.fix: Put the lid back on for 3 more minutes, then uncover and let them crisp again.

wrong.sign: The eggs are dry and rubbery
wrong.fix: The heat was too high. Next time, use medium-low and stir slowly. They're done as soon as no wet egg is left.

quiz.q: Which part do you cook first?
choices: The potatoes, because they take longest
quiz.explain: Start with the slowest part so everything finishes together.
Warmth and a little steam make tortillas soft enough to roll.

substitutions.note: Gluten-free tortillas are smaller and crack more easily. Warm them well, and use a little less filling in each.

steps.text: Rinse and peel the potatoes. Dice them into ½-inch cubes.
steps.tip: Cut a thin slice off one side first so the potato sits flat and can't roll.

steps.text: Heat the oil in the skillet over medium heat. Add the potatoes and {qty:salt} salt, stir, and put the lid on.
While the potatoes steam, crack the {n:egg} eggs into the medium bowl, add the salt for the eggs, and whisk until smooth.
Wash your hands with soap, and wipe the counter where the eggs were.
steps.tip: Raw egg can carry germs. Clean hands before you touch anything else.

steps.text: Take the lid off the potatoes. Cook, stirring every few minutes, until they're golden and crisp outside and soft inside.
steps.look: Golden brown on several sides, and a fork slides into a cube easily.

steps.text: Scoop the potatoes into the large bowl and cover it with foil.
Turn the heat to medium-high. Pinch the sausage into the pan in small pieces, straight from the package.
Throw away the package and wash your hands with hot, soapy water.
Cook the sausage, breaking it into small crumbles with the wooden spoon, until it's browned with no pink left.
Push the sausage into a pile and slide the thermometer into the middle. It needs to read at least 165°F. If it doesn't, cook 1 more minute and check again.
Scoop the sausage into the bowl with the potatoes and cover it again. Scrape any stuck bits out of the pan with the spatula.

Turn the heat down to medium-low and melt the butter in the pan. Pour in the eggs. Stir slowly with the spatula, pushing the eggs from the edges to the middle, until they're set in soft curds with no wet egg left.
Push the eggs into a pile and slide the thermometer into the middle. It needs to read at least 160°F. Then turn off the stove.
Wet a kitchen towel, wring it out, and wrap the stack of tortillas in it. Lay it on the plate and microwave until the tortillas are warm and soft.
steps.tip: Open the towel away from your face. The steam inside is hot.

steps.text: Lay one tortilla flat. In a line just below the middle, put a scoop of potatoes and sausage, a scoop of eggs, and a handful of cheese. Leave about 2 inches empty on each side.
steps.tip: Share the filling out evenly: look at how much is left, and how many tortillas.

steps.text: Fold the bottom edge up over the filling and tuck it under snugly. Fold both sides toward the middle, then roll away from you, keeping it tight. Set it seam side down. Roll the rest the same way.
steps.tip: Seam side down keeps it closed while the others get rolled.

steps.text: Serve the burritos warm, with salsa and sour cream on the side if you're using them.
